questions.title: Dispatch Method With Send
questions.description:
Define a Calculator class with add(a, b) and sub(a, b) methods. Read a method name string ('add' or 'sub') and two integers, then call the chosen method on a Calculator instance using send. Print the integer result.

Input Format:
Line 1: method name (add or sub). Line 2: two space-separated integers a b.

Output Format:
The integer result.

Constraints:
method in {add, sub}; -1000 <= a, b <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
class Calculator
  def add(a, b); a + b; end
  def sub(a, b); a - b; end
end

m = gets.chomp
a, b = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
c = Calculator.new
puts c.send(m, a, b)

questions.title: Define Dynamic Multiplier Methods
questions.description:
Use define_method to create methods double and triple on a Multiplier class. Read a method name ('double' or 'triple') and an integer n, then call the chosen method directly on a Multiplier instance and print the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: method name (double or triple). Line 2: integer n.

Output Format:
The integer result.

Constraints:
method in {double, triple}; -1000 <= n <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
class Multiplier
  define_method(:double) { |x| x * 2 }
  define_method(:triple) { |x| x * 3 }
end

cmd = gets.chomp
n = gets.to_i
m = Multiplier.new
result = cmd == "double" ? m.double(n) : m.triple(n)
puts result

questions.title: Robot Command Dispatcher

A robot exposes commands move, turn, and stop. Define a Robot class with move(d) returning 'Moved <d>m', turn(d) returning 'Turned <d>deg', and stop returning 'Stopped'. Read n then n command lines: each is either a single word 'stop' or 'op arg' (e.g. 'move 5'); dispatch each via send and print the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: a command (single word, or word + arg).

questions.title: Define Animal Sounds From Hash
questions.description:
An animal soundboard builds methods from a hash. Define an Animal class that uses a SOUNDS hash to define_method for each kind, returning the corresponding sound. Read a kind ('dog', 'cat', or 'bird'); call the matching method on an Animal instance and print the sound.

Input Format:
Line 1: kind (dog, cat, or bird).

Output Format:
The sound string.

Constraints:
kind in {dog, cat, bird}.
questions.sourcecode:
class Animal
  SOUNDS = { dog: "Woof", cat: "Meow", bird: "Chirp" }.freeze
  SOUNDS.each do |k, v|
    define_method(k) { v }
  end
end

a = Animal.new
k = gets.chomp
puts case k
when "dog" then a.dog
when "cat" then a.cat
when "bird" then a.bird
end

questions.title: Calculator Ops Dispatch With Send
questions.description:
A calculator supports four operations. Define a Calculator class with add(a,b), sub(a,b), mul(a,b), and div(a,b) where div returns 'ERR' on division by zero. Read n then n lines 'op a b' (op in add, sub, mul, div); dispatch each operation via send and print the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: 'op a b' with integers a b.

Output Format:
One result per line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; -1000 <= a, b <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
class Calculator
  def add(a, b); a + b; end
  def sub(a, b); a - b; end

end

n = gets.to_i
calc = Calculator.new

  puts calc.send(op, a.to_i, b.to_i)

  puts d.send(op, x.to_i)
end

questions.title: OpenStruct Like Bag Method Missing
questions.description:
Implement a Bag class mimicking OpenStruct. method_missing handles setter calls (name ending in =) by storing the value in an internal hash, and getter calls by returning the stored value or 'missing' if absent. Read n then n lines that are either 'set key value' or 'get key'; dispatch set/get via send and print results for each get.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: 'set key value' or 'get key'.

Output Format:
For each get: the stored value or 'missing'.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100; 1 <= key, value length <= 20.
questions.sampleinput1:
3
set name Alice
get name
get age
questions.sampleinput2:
4
set a 1
set b 2
get a
get b
questions.input3:
4
set score 10
get q
get score
get z
questions.sourcecode:
class Bag
  def initialize; @h = {}; end
  def method_missing(name, *args)
    n = name.to_s
    if n.end_with?("=")
      @h[n.chomp("=")] = args[0]
    else
      @h.key?(n) ? @h[n] : "missing"
    end
  end
end

b = Bag.new
n = gets.to_i
n.times do
  line = gets.chomp
  parts = line.split
  if parts[0] == "set"
    b.send("#{parts[1]}=", parts[2])
  else
    puts b.send(parts[1])
  end
end

questions.title: Dynamic Finder With Method Missing
questions.description:
A record finder supports dynamic find_by_X-style lookups via method_missing. Records are stored in a frozen DATA constant. method_missing handles names starting with 'find_' by extracting the field after the prefix and returning the id of the first matching record or 'not found'. Read n then n lines 'field:value'; for each, dispatch 'find_<field>' via send and print the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: 'field:value'.

Output Format:
One result per line (id string or 'not found').

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 1 <= field, value length <= 20.
questions.sourcecode:
class Finder
  DATA = [
    { "id" => "1", "name" => "Alice", "city" => "NYC" },
    { "id" => "2", "name" => "Bob", "city" => "LA" },
    { "id" => "3", "name" => "Carol", "city" => "NYC" }
  ].freeze
  def method_missing(name, *args)
    n = name.to_s
    if n.start_with?("find_")
      field = n[5..]
      row = DATA.find { |r| r[field] == args[0] }
      row ? row["id"] : "not found"
    else
      super
    end
  end
end

f = Finder.new
n = gets.to_i
n.times do
  line = gets.chomp
  field, value = line.split(":")
  puts f.send("find_#{field}", value)
end

questions.title: Record Find By With Respond To Override
questions.description:
A record class supports dynamic find_by_<field> queries via method_missing, and overrides respond_to? to report true for any find_by_ name. The frozen DATA constant holds three records. method_missing returns the comma-joined ids of all matching records, or 'none' if no match. Read n then n lines 'field:value'; for each, dispatch 'find_by_<field>' via send and print the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: 'field:value'.

Output Format:
One result per line: comma-joined ids or 'none'.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 1 <= field, value length <= 20.
questions.sourcecode:
class Record
  DATA = [
    { "id" => "1", "name" => "Alice", "age" => "30" },
    { "id" => "2", "name" => "Bob", "age" => "25" },
    { "id" => "3", "name" => "Carol", "age" => "30" }
  ].freeze

  def respond_to?(name)
    n = name.to_s
    n.start_with?("find_by_") ? true : super
  end

  def method_missing(name, *args)
    n = name.to_s
    if n.start_with?("find_by_")
      field = n.sub("find_by_", "")
      matches = DATA.select { |r| r[field] == args[0] }
      matches.empty? ? "none" : matches.map { |r| r["id"] }.join(",")
    else
      super
    end
  end
end

r = Record.new
n = gets.to_i
n.times do
  line = gets.chomp
  field, value = line.split(":")
  puts r.send("find_by_#{field}", value)
end

questions.title: QueryBuilder Methods With Class Eval
questions.description:
A query builder dynamically defines one method per operation name using class_eval and define_method. The OPS constant lists :select, :where, :order, :limit, :group. Each defined method returns '<op>(<arg>)'. Read n then n lines 'op arg' (op in select, where, order, limit, group); dispatch via send and print each result.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: 'op arg'.

Output Format:
One result per line: '<op>(<arg>)'.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 1 <= arg length <= 30.
questions.input1:
3
select id
where id=1
order name
questions.sourcecode:
class QueryBuilder
  OPS = [:select, :where, :order, :limit, :group].freeze
  class_eval do
    OPS.each do |op|
      define_method(op) { |arg| "#{op}(#{arg})" }
    end
  end
end

n = gets.to_i
q = QueryBuilder.new
n.times do
  op, arg = gets.split
  puts q.send(op, arg)
end

questions.title: Model Find By And Count By Missing
questions.description:
A model supports both find_by_<field> (returns first match id or 'nil') and count_by_<field> (returns count of matches) via method_missing, with respond_to? returning true for both prefixes. Records are passed in via the constructor. Read n then n lines 'op field value' (op in find_by, count_by); dispatch '<op>_<field>' via send and print the result.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: 'op field value'.

Output Format:
One result per line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 1 <= field, value length <= 20.
questions.sampleinput1:
3
find_by dept Eng
count_by dept Eng
find_by role Rep
questions.sampleinput2:
2
count_by dept Sales
find_by role QA
questions.input2:
3
count_by dept Eng
count_by dept Sales
find_by dept Sales
questions.input3:
2
find_by role Dev
count_by role Dev
questions.sourcecode:
class Model
  def initialize(data); @data = data; end
  def method_missing(name, *args)
    n = name.to_s
    if n.start_with?("find_by_")
      field = n.sub("find_by_", "")
      row = @data.find { |r| r[field] == args[0] }
      row ? row["id"] : "nil"
    elsif n.start_with?("count_by_")
      field = n.sub("count_by_", "")
      @data.count { |r| r[field] == args[0] }
    else
      super
    end
  end
  def respond_to?(name)
    n = name.to_s
    n.start_with?("find_by_") || n.start_with?("count_by_") || super
  end
end

data = [
  { "id" => "1", "dept" => "Eng", "role" => "Dev" },
  { "id" => "2", "dept" => "Eng", "role" => "QA" },
  { "id" => "3", "dept" => "Sales", "role" => "Rep" }
]

m = Model.new(data)
n = gets.to_i
n.times do
  line = gets.chomp
  op, field, value = line.split
  puts m.send("#{op}_#{field}", value)
end
